answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x target with settlement at peak. Rollback is blocked by compliance (security patch must stay). Regional failover risks losing in-flight customer writes during a peak settlement window — bad fit when the primary objective is preserving writes. Read-replica routing does not touch the write path. Circuit breakers would shed load but at peak settlement that means dropping customer writes. Adding capacity on the write path is the only intervention that addresses the symptom without threatening writes; write-path load is the bottleneck, not read load, so memory_b5 (read-replica relief for primary) is a partial precedent but not a direct template. memory_b1 (rollback cleared a spike) is tempting precedent but the current release cannot be reverted. Pulling memory_b1 to verify its exact context — including any caveats about when rollback helped vs. when other causes produced the spike — lets me rule out a similar-looking signature that actually points elsewhere. Pulling memory_b5 verifies whether the underlying mechanism that relieved the primary (offloading pressure) can be repurposed for the write path. Stop condition: if the capacity add does not bend the p99 curve inside a short observation window, reassess before any further action; sustained availability requires not committing to a second move prematurely.
